title: How Non-US Residents Can Open a Mercury or Relay Business Bank Account Without a SSN or ITIN
content:
# How Non-US Residents Can Open a Mercury or Relay Business Bank Account Without a SSN or ITIN

If you're a non-US resident running a US LLC, you already know the frustration: most banking guides assume you have a Social Security Number (SSN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN). You don't. And yet, Mercury and Relay are two platforms that have genuinely opened their doors to international founders — if you approach the application correctly.

This guide walks you through exactly what you need, what to expect, and how to avoid the mistakes that get applications rejected.

---

## Why US Business Banking Is Non-Negotiable for Your LLC

A US business bank account is not a "nice to have." It's the infrastructure that makes your LLC functional.

Without one, you can't:

- Accept USD payments from US clients or platforms like Stripe and PayPal
- Pay US-based contractors or vendors cleanly
- Separate personal and business finances (a legal requirement for LLC liability protection)
- Build a business credit history in the US

The good news: you don't need an SSN or ITIN to open accounts with Mercury or Relay. You need the right documents, the right LLC structure, and the right approach.

---

## Mercury vs. Relay: Which One Is Right for You?

Both platforms are fintech-based business banking solutions popular with startups and remote entrepreneurs. Here's how they compare at a glance:

| Feature | Mercury | Relay |
|---|---|---|
| **Non-US Resident Friendly** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **SSN / ITIN Required** | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **Monthly Fees** | $0 (base) | $0 (base) |
| **Physical Debit Card** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Virtual Cards** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Multiple Sub-Accounts** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (up to 20) |
| **ACH & Wire Transfers** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Stripe / PayPal Integration** | ✅ Strong | ✅ Good |
| **Best For** | Tech startups, SaaS | Service businesses, agencies |

> **Note:** Neither Mercury nor Relay is a traditional bank. Mercury is backed by Choice Financial Group and Evolve Bank & Trust (FDIC-insured). Relay is backed by Thread Bank (FDIC-insured). Your deposits are protected, but these are not chartered banks themselves.

---

## What You Actually Need Before You Apply

This is where most international founders get tripped up. Prepare everything before you touch the application form.

### 1. A Properly Formed US LLC

You must have a legally registered LLC in the United States. Both platforms require this.

- **Best states for non-residents:** Wyoming, Delaware, or New Mexico
- Your LLC must be active and in good standing
- You'll need your **Articles of Organization** (or Certificate of Formation)

> **Note:** If you haven't formed your LLC yet, start with our [LLC Guide](/llc-guide) before continuing. Applying for a bank account without a properly formed entity is a guaranteed rejection.

### 2. An EIN (Employer Identification Number)

This is your business tax ID — and it's the substitute for your SSN in the banking application process.

- Apply directly through the IRS (Form SS-4)
- Non-residents must apply by fax or mail — the online EIN application requires a US SSN
- Processing time: 4–6 weeks by fax, 8–12 weeks by mail
- Your EIN confirmation letter (CP-575) is the document banks want to see

> **Note:** Do not use third-party services that charge $200–$500 for EIN acquisition. The IRS issues EINs for free. See our [Start Here](/start-here) page for the exact process.

### 3. Your Passport (Government-Issued ID)

Both platforms require a valid, government-issued photo ID. Your passport is the cleanest option. Driver's licenses from non-US countries are accepted by some platforms but can cause friction.

### 4. Proof of Business Address (For Your LLC)

Your LLC needs a registered US address. This is typically your **registered agent's address** — not a personal address.

- A registered agent service address is accepted
- A virtual mailbox address (e.g., Anytime Mailbox, PostScan Mail) is also accepted
- A UPS Store or similar address may cause flags — use a legitimate virtual office or registered agent

### 5. Operating Agreement

Both Mercury and Relay may request your LLC's Operating Agreement, especially if there are multiple members or if your application triggers a manual review.

- For single-member LLCs, a basic Operating Agreement is sufficient
- Make sure it lists you as the sole member and manager
- Dates and signatures matter — don't submit a blank template

### 6. Beneficial Ownership Information

Under US FinCEN regulations, both platforms are required to collect information about who owns and controls the business. As a non-US resident, you'll need to:

- Confirm you own 25% or more of the LLC
- Provide your country of residence
- Submit your passport as identity verification

---

## How to Apply for a Mercury Business Bank Account (Step-by-Step)

### Step 1: Go to Mercury.com and Start Your Application

Click "Open an Account." You'll be asked to enter your business email and create a password. Do not use a personal email — use a dedicated business email (yourname@yourdomain.com looks professional and reduces friction).

### Step 2: Select Your Business Type

Choose **LLC** as your entity type. Mercury will then ask for:

- Legal business name (must match your Articles of Organization exactly)
- State of formation
- EIN

### Step 3: Enter Business Details

Fill in:

- Business address (use your registered agent or virtual mailbox address)
- Business description (be specific — "SaaS product for marketing agencies" is better than "software company")
- Expected monthly revenue and transaction volume (be honest and realistic)

### Step 4: Submit Owner / Beneficial Ownership Information

This is where you enter your personal details as a non-US resident:

- Full legal name
- Country of residence (your home country — not the US)
- Date of birth
- Passport number and expiration date
- You'll be prompted to upload a photo of your passport

### Step 5: Upload Your Documents

Have these ready to upload:

- ✅ EIN Confirmation Letter (CP-575 or 147C letter)
- ✅ Articles of Organization / Certificate of Formation
- ✅ Passport (clear photo, all four corners visible)
- ✅ Operating Agreement (if requested)

### Step 6: Wait for Review

Mercury typically reviews applications within **1–5 business days**. You may receive:

- **Instant approval** (common for well-prepared applications)
- **A request for additional documents** (respond within 48 hours to avoid delays)
- **A rejection** (see the troubleshooting section below)

---

## How to Apply for a Relay Business Bank Account (Step-by-Step)

### Step 1: Go to RelayFi.com and Create an Account

Click "Open an Account." Enter your business email and create a password. Like Mercury, use a professional business email.

### Step 2: Enter Your Business Information

You'll be asked for:

- Legal business name (must match your LLC documents exactly)
- Business entity type (select LLC)
- State of formation
- EIN
- Business industry and description

### Step 3: Add Your Personal Information as the Business Owner

As a non-US resident:

- Select your country of residence
- Enter your passport details
- Confirm you do not have an SSN or ITIN (Relay's form accommodates this)

### Step 4: Upload Your Documents

Relay typically requests:

- ✅ EIN Confirmation Letter
- ✅ Articles of Organization
- ✅ Government-issued ID (passport preferred)
- ✅ Operating Agreement (for manual reviews)

### Step 5: Choose Your Account Structure

This is one of Relay's standout features: you can open **up to 20 sub-accounts** under one business. Set up separate accounts for:

- Operating expenses
- Tax reserves (set aside 25–30% of revenue here)
- Owner's draws / payroll
- Emergency fund

### Step 6: Await Approval

Relay's review timeline is similar to Mercury: **1–5 business days** for most applications. Complex ownership structures or high-risk industries may take longer.

---

## Common Reasons Applications Get Rejected (And How to Avoid Them)

Getting rejected is demoralizing — but it's almost always avoidable. Here are the most common reasons non-residents get rejected and exactly what to do instead.

### ❌ Mismatch Between Business Name and Documents

If your Articles of Organization say "Horizon Digital LLC" but you type "Horizon Digital" in the application, the system flags it. Use your **exact legal business name**, including the LLC designation.

### ❌ Vague Business Description

"Online business" or "consulting" are red flags. Be specific. Write out what you do, who your customers are, and how money flows through the business.

> **Example:** Instead of "consulting," write "digital marketing consulting for e-commerce brands in the US and Europe, primarily B2B, average transaction $1,500–$5,000."

### ❌ No EIN or Using the Wrong Document

Your SS-4 application is not the same as your EIN confirmation. Mercury and Relay want the **CP-575 letter** (or a 147C letter if you've lost your CP-575). Do not submit your SS-4 form.

### ❌ High-Risk Business Categories

Both platforms avoid certain industries. If your business involves:

- Cryptocurrency trading or exchanges
- Gambling or gaming
- Adult content
- Firearms or tobacco

…you will likely be rejected. Check each platform's acceptable use policy before applying.

### ❌ Suspicious or Mismatched Addresses

Using a personal residential address in a country outside the US for your LLC's business address — when your LLC is registered in Wyoming — can trigger a manual review. Keep your LLC address consistent with your registered agent or virtual mailbox.

### ❌ Rushing the Application

Don't fill out the form quickly and carelessly. Every field matters. Take 30–45 minutes, have all your documents open, and review everything before submitting.

---

## What Happens After You're Approved

Once approved, here's your immediate action list:

- [ ] **Set up your account login with 2FA** (mandatory for security)
- [ ] **Order your physical debit card** (ships to most international addresses)
- [ ] **Set up virtual cards** for online subscriptions and vendor payments
- [ ] **Connect your payment processor** (Stripe, PayPal, or Wise Business) to your new account
- [ ] **Share your account details** (routing number + account number) with clients for ACH payments
- [ ] **Set up sub-accounts** for tax reserves (especially if using Relay)
- [ ] **Download your account statements** monthly for bookkeeping

---

## Mercury vs. Relay: Which Should You Open First?

Here's our honest recommendation:

**Open both.** They're free. There's no downside to having two accounts.

Use **Mercury** as your primary operating account — it has cleaner integrations with Stripe, Brex, and other tools commonly used by SaaS and digital product businesses.

Use **Relay** for cash flow management — its multi-account structure is genuinely excellent for separating tax reserves, operating expenses, and savings. It's the closest thing to the "profit first" banking system without extra cost.

> **Note:** Having two US business bank accounts also provides redundancy. If one account is ever frozen or flagged for review, your business doesn't stop.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I open a Mercury or Relay account if I live in a restricted country?

Both platforms restrict residents of certain countries due to US sanctions and banking regulations. Countries commonly restricted include Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Syria, and others on the OFAC sanctions list. Check current restrictions on each platform's website before applying.

### Do I need to visit the US to open these accounts?

No. Both Mercury and Relay are fully remote applications. You never need to set foot in the US.

### Can I use a nominee or third party to open the account on my behalf?

No. Both platforms require the actual beneficial owner to apply. Using a nominee or proxy is a violation of their terms and constitutes fraud under US banking law.

### What if my application is rejected?

Request a reason in writing. Gather any missing documents. Wait 30 days before reapplying. Consider reaching out to their support teams — both Mercury and Relay have responsive customer support and can sometimes reverse a rejection or guide you to reapply correctly.

### Can I receive international wire transfers into these accounts?

Yes. Both Mercury and Relay support incoming international wires. Mercury also offers outgoing international wires in select currencies. For paying international contractors or receiving payments in non-USD currencies, pairing your account with **Wise Business** is highly recommended.

---

## Your Next Steps

Getting a US business bank account as a non-resident is entirely achievable — but it requires doing things in the right order with the right documentation.

**Here's your sequence:**

1. ✅ Form your US LLC → [LLC Guide](/llc-guide)
2. ✅ Obtain your EIN from the IRS
3. ✅ Prepare your documents (CP-575, Articles of Organization, Passport, Operating Agreement)
4. ✅ Apply to Mercury and Relay with complete, accurate information
5. ✅ Set up your accounts and connect your payment processors
